title: Pond liner and leak inspection
audience: Pond and water-feature technicians who inspect liners, edges, outlets and pump fittings for leaks and damage
learningOutcomes: Inspect a pond liner, its edges, penetrations, outlets and pump fittings for signs of leaks and damage
Carry out a bucket test to separate evaporation from a leak, and record the result with its conditions
Identify liner materials and conditions that increase the risk of damage, and report them without recommending a product
Work on liners and edges without damaging the liner or creating a fall, crush or electrical hazard

instruction.heading: Scope: maintenance and inspection, not construction
instruction.body: This lesson covers inspection, testing and reporting on a pond that already exists. Building a new pond, excavating a pit, laying a new liner or reshaping a pond is a separate course and is outside the scope of this lesson. If a client needs a new liner or structural work, record the findings, refer the work and quote it under the business's approved method. Replacing a liner is not a routine maintenance task for this course.

instruction.heading: Where pond leaks occur
instruction.body: Pond leaks usually appear at the liner edges, at seams and joins, at places where pipes or outlets pass through the liner, at the waterline where ultraviolet light and wear damage the liner, under rocks, and where tree roots push the liner upward. Liners also fail where they have been stretched, because a stretched liner thins and cracks over time. Pumps, valves, fittings and the connections to a skimmer or bog filter can leak too. Inspect each of these in turn rather than looking only at the water surface, because a leak can be hidden below the water or in the surround. Note any sign of soil or sand washing in along an edge, since that often points to a gap in the edge or the liner beneath it.

instruction.heading: The liner itself: materials and condition
instruction.body: A liner should be rated for ultraviolet light and for the frost conditions of the site, otherwise it can become brittle or lose its seams. Tarpaulins and similar sheeting should not be used as a pond liner, because some contain heavy metals that can harm fish and plants. Some laminated textured liners can separate their layers in weather, causing leaks, so record the material if it can be identified. Report the material and its condition, and do not recommend a brand or product. Avoid stretching the liner during inspection or cleaning, because stretching shortens its life. Where a liner is covered by gravel or slope protection, record how much of the liner is covered before you start, because covered areas are harder to inspect.

instruction.heading: The bucket test
instruction.body: A bucket test separates evaporation from a leak. Place a bucket on a step inside the pond so that its water level is close to the pond's level, mark the water level inside and outside the bucket, and leave it for the same period under the same conditions. If the water level in the pond drops more than the level in the bucket, the loss is more likely to be a leak or an outlet fault. Record the start and finish times, the level drop inside and outside the bucket in millimetres, the air temperature in Celsius, the rain and the wind. Repeat the test if the first result is unclear, and report the result rather than guessing. A short test is evidence of loss, but it does not show where the leak is.

instruction.heading: Inspecting safely and recording findings
instruction.body: Do not walk on a liner in shoes that may puncture it. Use soft-soled footwear with rounded soles, or boards, and keep sharp tools away from the liner. Lift rocks one at a time with a plan, because a rock can fall and cause a crush injury. Keep walkways and edges clear, and be careful on wet edges and steep banks. Work near electrical pumps only after the power is isolated and proven off, and do not use a damaged cord. Connection work and wiring are licensed work in many circumstances; in New South Wales, wiring work is licensed or certified work at any price. Record what you inspected and what you found, including the location of any damage, the method of the test and the result. Do not certify the pond as watertight after a visual check. A bucket test over a short period supports a finding, but a repair is a separate scope that the client must approve.

procedure: Confirm the work order and whether a repair is in scope. Record that new construction is not included.
Record the weather, the water level, the air temperature in Celsius and the time.
Inspect the liner edges, seams, penetrations, waterline, rocks, tree-root pressure and outlets, one at a time.
Carry out the bucket test and record the level drop inside and outside the bucket.
Isolate and check pumps, fittings and connections without damaging the liner, and refer any electrical fault.
Record the findings with the location of each defect, and take photographs where the business requires them.
Refer any repair and report the result to the owner in writing, without certifying the pond as watertight.

workedExamples.situation: An owner says the pond has dropped about 40 millimetres overnight in still, mild weather and asks for the liner to be repaired.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the technician do before quoting a repair?
workedExamples.reasoning: The technician carries out a bucket test over the next period, records the weather and the drop inside and outside the bucket, and inspects the liner, penetrations, outlets and pump fittings. The repair is quoted only after the leak is located or the test result is clear enough to support it. The technician does not certify the pond as watertight, and does not replace the liner, which is outside this course.

workedExamples.situation: While checking a pond, the technician finds a wet patch at the pump outlet and an exposed cable near the water.
workedExamples.reasoning: The technician isolates the pump and does not touch the cable or the connection, because connection work is licensed in many circumstances. The wet outlet is recorded and referred for repair. The exposed cable is reported to the owner as an electrical hazard, with its location, and the referral is recorded. The lesson does not authorise any electrical work.

equipmentAndPpe: Bucket and marker for the water level
Measuring tape or ruler in millimetres
Soft-soled footwear with rounded soles, or boards

commonErrors.error: Assuming a leak from a single look at the water.
commonErrors.prevention: Run a bucket test and record the result with its conditions.

commonErrors.error: Walking on the liner in shoes that can puncture it.
commonErrors.prevention: Use soft-soled footwear with rounded soles, or boards.

commonErrors.error: Certifying the pond as watertight after an inspection.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the result. Do not certify watertightness.

commonErrors.error: Working on a pump connection without isolating the power.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate, prove off and refer any electrical fault.

commonErrors.error: Recommending a liner product or brand during an inspection.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the material and condition, and refer the choice of any replacement to the client and the approved method.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical connection and wiring work at water features is licensed work in many circumstances. In New South Wales, wiring work needs a licence or certificate at any price, and the page treats putting in, fixing, changing, taking out or extending an electrical installation as wiring work. The page excludes electrical equipment operating at not more than 50 volts AC or 120 volts ripple-free DC (NSW Government electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). Mains-powered pond pump connections are above that limit. This lesson does not grant any licence.
Lifting rocks and working at pond edges carries crush, slip and fall risks. Plan each lift, keep walkways clear and do not work on a wet edge without grip.
Repairs to a liner, and any structural work on the pond, are outside this course. They require the client's approval and the business's approved method.

qualityStandard: Bucket test completed with recorded conditions, times, levels and result
Inspection covers liner, seams, penetrations, waterline, outlets, rocks and pump fittings
No watertightness is certified without a test that supports it
documentationEvidence: Bucket test record with times, levels in millimetres, weather and air temperature in Celsius
Inspection findings with the location of each defect
Repair referral and any quote reference
summary: Leaks hide at edges, seams, penetrations, the waterline and outlets, so inspect each in turn.
The bucket test separates evaporation from loss, but it does not locate a leak.
Protect the liner when you walk and lift, and isolate power before you touch any pump fitting.
Record the result. Do not certify the pond as watertight, and refer repairs and any new construction.

knowledgeChecks.question: A pond has lost water overnight. What is the best first step?
options: Carry out a bucket test under the same conditions and record the result
Add water and assume it is evaporation, since the summer is hot
Replace the whole liner straight away, since it is probably old
Certify the pond as watertight after a glance at the surface

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the technician avoid walking on the liner in ordinary shoes?
options: It is only a colour rule

knowledgeChecks.question: A pump connection is wet and a cable is exposed. What is the correct action?
options: Tape the cable and leave it for now, since the pump still works fine
Open the connection box to check the wiring before any action is taken
Isolate the power, do not touch the connection, and refer the electrical work
Ignore it because the pump is working and the water is clear today
